name: X2Go
description: A fully open-source terminal-server-style remote desktop built on the original open NX libraries, transported entirely over SSH. Its signature feature is session persistence — suspend a full Linux desktop session and resume it later from anywhere, apps still running.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Strictly tied to X11/Xorg; the server side does not support Wayland sessions at all

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration; works over any network reachability, including a VPN like Tailscale

Open Source.comment: Fully open source (GPL), built on the original open NX protocol libraries

Microphone Passthrough.comment: Audio forwarding is host-to-client (playback); client-mic-to-host passthrough isn't documented

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: Link-quality profile (modem/ISDN/ADSL/WAN/LAN) is manually selected per session, not auto-detected

Multi-User Sessions.comment: Runs as a terminal-server: multiple independent concurrent user sessions per server are core to its design

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: Uses NX-derived differential/image compression rather than a video codec pipeline

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Not a video-streaming tool; performance is measured in responsiveness, not FPS

Pre-Login Access.comment: Creates a new virtual X11 desktop session rather than unlocking the physical machine's actual login screen

No Account Required.comment: Just needs SSH credentials on the target machine; no cloud account of any kind

Shared Clipboard.comment: Clipboard mode (both/server/client/none) is configurable per session for security

2FA / MFA.comment: No built-in 2FA layer; relies entirely on whatever SSH authentication (password/key) is configured

Windows: Host.comment: The X2Go server only runs on Linux

macOS: Host.comment: The X2Go server only runs on Linux

macOS: Client.comment: Some reported window-resizing quirks on recent macOS releases

Linux X11: Host.comment: The only supported host platform, and the project's native environment

Web Browser: Client.comment: Native Qt-based client only, no official browser client

Free Tier.comment: Entirely free and open source, no paid tiers at all

Enterprise.comment: No official paid/enterprise tier; purely community-maintained
